newsitem.title: TANZANIA: SOCCER-TANZANIA AND NAMIBIA BATTLE TO GOALLESS DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TANZANIA AND NAMIBIA BATTLE TO GOALLESS DRAW.

text.p: Tanzania and Namibia played out a goalless draw in their Cosafa Castle Cup final round group match in Mwanza on Saturday, both spurning opportunities but fighting out a lively midfield battle.
It was the first game for both teams in the league competition of the new southern African competition, which also features Malawi, Mozambique and Zambia.

Tanzania, who have won just one of their last 15 matches, saw efforts from Idelphonce Amlima and debutant John Masamaki Thomas sail wide of the target while Ruben van Wyk and Eliphas Shivute squandered breakaway opportunities for the Namibian vistors.
Amlima was off target with two close-range headers while substitute Thomas blasted a left-footed shot over the bar.

Hesitation cost Van Wyk a chance for Namibia early in the second half when he beat the offside trap but was caught by Tanzanian captain Hussein Marsha, while Shivute's breakaway effort was brilliantly stopped by Tanzanian substitute goalkeeper Riffat Sid.
The game produced a plenty of exciting build-ups in midfield but few telling passes were produced to offer any clear-out goalscoring opportunities.
Namibia and Tanzania both collected a point from the game but trail Zambia in the standings.
The competition is being run under the auspices of the Confederation of Southern African Football Associations (Cosafa).
